chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! Is the Ziyarah of Al-Reza (peace be upon him) superior or the Ziyarah of Abu Abdullah Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'The Ziyarah of my father is superior, and that is because all people visit Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and my father is visited only by the special ones from the Shiah.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Reza (the title of Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Reza)

ai.seo_question: Which is more virtuous: visiting Imam Al-Reza or Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Reza (as) distinguishes between the universal appeal of Imam Al-Husayn’s shrine, which attracts all people, and the exclusive, intimate devotion of the *khawass* (elite) Shia to his own resting place. This comparison highlights a theological nuance in Shia tradition: while the martyrdom of Imam Al-Husayn serves as a global symbol of resistance and faith, the Ziyarah of Imam Al-Reza represents a deeper, specialized spiritual connection reserved for the core community. The distinction underscores the varying degrees of spiritual merit based on the depth of the visitor's faith rather than the physical location alone.
